name: Correlation (Pearson / Spearman) with significance test
when_to_use: Two metric variables (Pearson, linear relationship) or at least ordinal ones (Spearman, monotonic relationship); measure the strength and test the significance of the association before other modeling.
notes: Measures whether two numeric variables rise and fall together, and whether that relationship is strong enough to trust. Applications: check whether marketing spend tracks sales before running a regression.

expected_input.question: Do two numeric variables vary together, and is the relationship strong enough to trust?

pdca_use: Plan/Check phase: measure whether two indicators vary together (and how much) before proposing an action — auditable diagnosis, not a predictive model.

plain_explanation.purpose: Measures how much two things vary together, from -1 to +1.
plain_explanation.when_to_use_plain: When you want to know whether two numbers move together, without claiming that one causes the other.
plain_explanation.example: See whether ad spend and sales rise together.
plain_explanation.diagram: +1: rise together | 0: no relationship | -1: one rises, the other falls
